summary: Deferred variant activation leads to second-tier routing and serial cold-starts causing elevated p95/p99 for customer requests
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reports intermittent high tail latency and occasional 504s starting after a traffic shift on 2026-03-09. Impact: Customer experiences increased p95/p99 generation latency for a core search summarization endpoint, impacting live users and batch jobs. Environment: Dedicated tenant in prod (us-east-1), route r-7a9c pinned to redwood-ggml-13B:v2026-02-28.

Observed behavior: During sustained ramp (approx 300->1200 qps over 10m) the platform began diverting ~18% of requests to a deprioritized CPU fallback variant and another ~12% to a newly-provisioned quantized variant that had not finished warmup. These routes showed serial warmups: each routed replica performed a multi-step KV and tensor cache population that blocked other warmups, producing queuing and per-request additional 400-1200ms. Customer metrics: p50 steady at ~120ms, p95 rose from 420ms to 1.8s, p99 spikes to 3.6s, and a 504 rate of ~0.7% for the 30m window.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady traffic at 300 qps for 20m to route r-7a9c. 2) Gradually ramp to 1200 qps over 10 minutes while monitoring Console -> Routes -> r-7a9c and Grafana panels 'serving_latency' and 'fallback_routing'. 3) Observe variant activation events in logs and look for 'activation_deferred' markers in routing-service traces.

Expected behavior: Newly-provisioned variants should warm in parallel up to configured concurrency gates or be shielded from receiving production traffic until KV cache is populated and model KV warmup completes. Fallback routing should prefer warm replicas with KV cache hot so as to avoid serial coldstart penalty.

Initial hypothesis: A recent change to the routing gating logic treats newly-created quantized variants as 'eligible' earlier than before when cluster capacity is constrained. This caused the scheduler to perform a 'best-effort' activation that returned a ready flag before KV warmup finished, allowing the routing layer to send traffic. Additionally, capacity gating deferred activation of a memory-optimized variant, moving traffic to a CPU fallback variant with higher per-request setup cost.

Relevant logs and dashboards: Console route: r-7a9c. Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/XyZ/serving-latency?var-route=r-7a9c. S3 logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/us-east/routing/2026-03-09/r-7a9c/*.log. Traces: https://jaeger.redwood.ai/trace/7f3b2... (see spans tagged routing-service/activation_deferred).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 14:22 - Support triage: Received alert from BrightDocs via support channel (#support) and verified increased tail latency in customer's telemetry. 2026-03-09 14:40 - On-call routed to Samir. Observed repeated log entries 'activation_deferred: reason=capacity_gate' correlated with time windows of autoscaler activity. 2026-03-09 15:05 - Replayed traffic pattern in staging and reproduced serial warmup behavior when route concurrency gate was set to 8 and autoscaler returned new replicas with 'ready=true' before KV warmup completion. 2026-03-10 09:12 - Engineering confirmed a change in routing-service PR 665 modified eligibility check to only require 'process_ready' rather than 'kv_warm_complete' under heavy autoscale conditions. 2026-03-11 11:30 - Experiment: temporarily increased gate to require 'kv_warm_complete' for eligible=true; tail latency returned to baseline in canary cluster.
resolution: Applied emergency config rollback on 2026-03-12 02:15 UTC to restore pre-PR-665 gating behavior (require kv_warm_complete before routing). Deployed a hotfix to routing-service (PR 723) to add a delayed-activation grace window: newly-created replicas are marked ineligible until KV warmup AND model-cache metrics pass thresholds or until a 30s shield expires. Monitored customer route for 48h; p95 fell back to ~400ms and 504s returned to <0.05%.
workaround: For impacted customers: pin route to a known-warm variant or temporarily increase 'min_warm_replicas' in Dedicated config. For BrightDocs we pinned to redwood-ggml-13B:v2026-02-14 and configured a 2x warm replica buffer while fix deployed.
next_steps: 1) Backfill automated test coverage for route eligibility that simulates KV warmup gating under autoscaler churn. 2) Add a dashboard alert for 'activation_deferred' spikes and a playbook link. 3) Consider adding per-tenant warm replica buffer controls for Dedicated customers. 4) Postmortem to be drafted and linked to this ticket. Owner: Samir. Target: postmortem draft by 2026-03-18.
